prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but I need a bit more information to recommend specific lawyers. Meanwhile, here’s practical, reliable guidance so you can quickly find the right attorney for a Pleasanton (Alameda County) car-accident injury case.

First: quick questions for you
- How badly were you injured (minor soft-tissue vs. fractures, surgery, permanent injury)?
- Who was at fault / was there a police report?
- Have you already spoken to an insurance company or signed anything?
- Are you still getting medical treatment?
- Do you want a local Pleasanton/Bay Area lawyer, or is any California personal-injury attorney fine?

If you want, tell me your answers and I can narrow recommendations.

Immediate steps you should take now
- Get medical care and follow all treatment instructions (important for health and your claim).
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, injuries, scene; dashcam/video; witness names/contacts.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other driver’s insurer without an attorney.
- Keep all medical bills, records, repair estimates, pay stubs (lost wages), receipts.
- Obtain the police report number and insurer contact info.
- Note: California’s general statute of limitations for personal injury is 2 years from the accident date — act promptly. Claims against public entities often require an administrative claim much sooner (often 6 months), so consult quickly if a government vehicle or entity is involved.

How to choose the right lawyer (what to look for)
- Relevant experience: specializes in car-accident / personal-injury cases, with experience handling injuries like yours.
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but pick someone who can and will take a case to trial if necessary.
- Track record: consistent settlements/verdicts in cases similar to yours.
- Communication: responsive, explains strategy and timelines in plain language.
- Fee structure: most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (commonly ~33%–40% of recovery). Ask about who pays costs (filing fees, experts) and whether the percentage changes if case goes to trial.
- Resources: firm should have access to medical experts, accident reconstruction, and litigation support if needed.
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Alameda County courts, insurers, and local medical providers helps.

Where to find attorneys
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.
- State Bar of California website — verify license and disciplinary record.
- Lawyer-rating sites (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Yelp) — use reviews as a starting point, not the only factor.
- Personal referrals from friends/family who had similar cases.

Questions to ask at (free) consultations
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? Results?
- Do you go to trial or mainly settle?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?
- What is your fee and what costs will I owe if we don’t recover?
- What’s your estimated timeline and likely range of recovery (based on details)?
- How often will you update me and by what method?
Bring these documents to the consultation
- Police report (if available), photos, medical records, bills, wage-loss documentation, insurance correspondence, vehicle repair estimates, witness info.

Red flags to avoid
- Promises of a specific settlement amount upfront.
- Pressure to sign immediately or give recorded statements to insurers.
- Poor responsiveness in the consult — you want someone who answers promptly.
- No contingency arrangement or unclear fee terms.

If you want specific local names
I can compile a short list of Pleasanton/Bay Area personal-injury attorneys for you to call if you’d like — tell me:
- Your ZIP or Pleasanton neighborhood,
- Whether you prefer small firm vs. big firm,
- Any other preferences (languages, weekend availability).

Would you like me to search and provide 3–5 local attorneys to contact? If so, give me the ZIP or confirm you want me to proceed and I’ll prepare a shortlist plus a sample message/phone script you can use.
